tracker_name: Political Violence and Social Cohesion Tracker
_schema_note: Append one object to weeks[] per run. Never edit a past week's original scores — add a retrospective_revision instead. See protocol.md Section 12.

indicators.name: Politically motivated violence
indicators.note: DOJ indicted eight men on murder/terrorism-conspiracy charges over a foiled drone-and-sniper plot targeting President Trump, VP Vance, and other officials at a White House UFC event; separately, a Manhattan arson attack on a federal building housing ICE offices was attributed by one outlet to an anti-ICE motive (single-sourced, flagged for corroboration).

indicators.name: Threats against officials/candidates/workers/judges
indicators.note: Supreme Court Justices Barrett and Kagan testified before Congress July 14 warning of a sharp rise in threats against the Court, including a swatting incident targeting Barrett; Capitol Police have logged over 5,000 threats against Members of Congress and staff in the past year.

indicators.name: Hate crimes and bias-motivated violence
indicators.note: No new dated incident this week; baseline held elevated given documented anti-Semitic incidents (synagogue arsons) and DOJ's Anti-Semitism Advisory Committee earlier in 2026.

indicators.name: Extremist mobilization
indicators.note: State Department hosted a ministerial on 'the resurgence of political terrorism' July 16, characterizing the threat as driven primarily by far-left networks; independent monitors (Bridging Divides Initiative) describe political violence risk as broadly worsening rather than concentrated on one side — the divergence in framing is itself notable.

indicators.name: Incitement and normalization
indicators.note: Analysis pieces (Brennan Center, CNN, Lawfare) argue the administration's domestic-terrorism framework (the Bondi memo, NSPM-7, the Antifa designation) defines political violence as an exclusively left-wing phenomenon rather than condemning violent rhetoric evenhandedly — treated here as a normalization concern; the underlying policy documents are verifiable, the characterization of their effect is more interpretive and flagged accordingly.

indicators.name: Protest-related violence
indicators.note: A nationwide 'day of action' on July 18 protesting ICE-related deaths was overwhelmingly peaceful mass protest (not scored as violence per protocol Section 4.4); isolated exceptions included a clash at a Scarborough, Maine ICE facility and the Manhattan arson incident noted above.

indicators.name: Weapons/plot activity
indicators.note: Reflects the same foiled White House UFC plot noted above — the group allegedly planned to use explosives-laden drones and firearms, indicating continued sophistication in plot planning; not scored as a separate incident from indicator 1.

indicators.name: Cross-partisan social trust
indicators.note: A UC San Diego survey found confidence that 2026 midterm votes will be counted accurately fell to 60% from 77% just after the 2024 election, with trust declining across all party lines (Republicans -17pts, independents -16pts, Democrats -13pts).

indicators.name: Civic and community engagement
indicators.note: No new data this week; carried forward at baseline.

indicators.name: De-escalation and bridging efforts
indicators.note: Princeton's Bridging Divides Initiative continues active bystander-intervention and de-escalation training programs and published a 2026 outlook identifying resilience strategies, though this reflects an ongoing program rather than a new event this week.

indicators.name: Leadership rhetoric and cross-aisle condemnation
indicators.note: Multiple analyses describe the administration characterizing political violence as a one-sided, left-wing problem rather than condemning violent rhetoric evenhandedly across the spectrum — the clearest negative signal in this week's SCI reading.

indicators.name: Law-enforcement and prosecutorial response
indicators.note: The FBI and DOJ successfully disrupted the White House UFC plot before it could be carried out and indicted all eight alleged participants, demonstrating real investigative and prosecutorial capacity; this week's evidence doesn't test even-handed application across ideological targets.

indicators.name: Local news and information ecosystem health
indicators.note: YouGov's 2026 Trust in Media survey found stark partisan bifurcation in outlet trust (an 85-point gap between Democrats and Republicans on both CNN and Fox News), consistent with a fragmented rather than shared information environment.

indicators.name: Institutional trust in elections/courts as fair arbiters
indicators.note: Same UC San Diego survey shows declining confidence in accurate vote counting across all parties heading into the midterms.

weeks.relationship_note: Real threat activity this week — a disrupted mass-casualty plot against the president and VP, rising threats against the judiciary — sits against a social fabric that is fraying on trust and leadership condemnation, but law enforcement's successful plot disruption and active civil-society de-escalation work are keeping the strain from becoming acute.

event_log.target: President Trump, VP Vance, and other officials/attendees at a White House UFC event
event_log.action: DOJ indicted eight men on murder and terrorism-conspiracy charges over an alleged foiled plot to attack the event using explosives-laden drones and firearms; arrests occurred across several states over the preceding weeks, with the final suspect arrested in West Virginia the week of this report.
event_log.notes: Indictment reported July 9-10, just before this reporting window, but the eighth and final arrest fell within the window (per NBC reporting) and the case's severity and ongoing legal proceedings make it clearly relevant to this week's assessment. Stated ideological motive of the defendants was not clearly established in available sourcing as of this report — classified as disputed/unclear rather than attributed to a specific side.

event_log.actor: Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan
event_log.action: Testified before Congress in a rare appearance, warning of a sharp rise in threats against the Court and requesting increased security funding; Barrett described being sent home with a bulletproof vest after a swatting incident.
event_log.notes: Bipartisan appearance by justices appointed by different presidents; framed as a shared institutional concern rather than a partisan complaint.

event_log.action: Coordinated 'day of action' protests in dozens of cities nationwide following two fatal shootings during ICE encounters (Biddeford, ME and Houston, TX); overwhelmingly peaceful, with isolated exceptions including a clash outside a Scarborough, ME ICE facility and a Manhattan arson attack on a federal building housing ICE offices, the latter attributed to an anti-ICE motive by one partisan-leaning outlet (uncorroborated by wire services as of this report).
event_log.notes: Per protocol Section 4.4, the large peaceful protest turnout itself is not scored as violence; only the isolated clash and arson incident are. The arson's political-motive characterization comes from a single partisan-leaning source and should be treated as unconfirmed pending corroboration.

event_log.actor: US Department of State (Secretary Marco Rubio)
event_log.target: Domestic and international framing of political violence
event_log.action: Hosted a ministerial on 'the resurgence of political terrorism,' characterizing the threat as driven primarily by organized far-left networks.
event_log.notes: Scored under SCI rather than PVEI: the concern here is one-sided framing undermining evenhanded cross-aisle condemnation of violence, not a claim about the underlying threat data itself, which independent monitors describe as broader than one ideological direction.

weeks.trajectory_note: This is the first tracked week, so there is no prior baseline for week-over-week movement; all changes and arrows are set to zero/steady accordingly. The baseline picture shows genuinely serious threat activity — a disrupted mass-casualty plot against the president and vice president, and Supreme Court justices publicly warning of rising threats — running alongside clear strain in the social fabric: declining cross-partisan trust in elections, a starkly bifurcated media-trust landscape, and, most notably, a federal leadership posture that critics across several outlets describe as characterizing political violence as a one-sided problem rather than condemning it evenhandedly. The most important positive counterweight this week is that law enforcement's response to the concrete, high-severity plot was fast and effective. The clearest thing to watch going forward is whether the administration's domestic-terrorism framework translates into uneven enforcement over time — that would be the gate that most changes this tracker's trajectory.

indicators.name: Politically motivated violence
indicators.note: No new completed, attempted, or foiled politically motivated attack or plot was identified in vetted sourcing this week (contrast with last tracked week's foiled White House UFC plot); indicator eases from Escalating to Warning on the absence of a fresh high-severity incident, not on any reduction of the underlying case, which remains in active prosecution.

indicators.name: Threats against officials/candidates/workers/judges
indicators.note: DHS General Counsel James Percival publicly named four sitting federal district judges in a 'Worst of the Worst, District Judge Edition' social-media series, accusing them of 'open defiance' and 'naked political activism'; U.S. Marshals Service data cited in coverage shows 564 threats against judges in FY2025 and 370 already in FY2026 as of July 1, and Judge Esther Salas — whose son was murdered in a 2020 attack motivated by a litigant's grievance with her rulings — publicly warned the naming-by-name campaign could inspire similar violence.

indicators.name: Hate crimes and bias-motivated violence
indicators.note: Prosecution continued this week in the July 23 Upper West Side double stabbing of a Jewish man and an Asian man (Raul Morales, charged with multiple hate-crime counts and held without bail); the underlying attack predates this reporting window but its prosecutorial status carried into it. No new dated hate-crime incident was identified within the window itself.

indicators.name: Extremist mobilization
indicators.note: No significant new evidence of organized extremist recruitment or coordinated mobilization surfaced this week; scattered background items (e.g., local political figures with past militia/'sovereign citizen'-adjacent affiliations) do not rise to a systemic signal. Carried at baseline.

indicators.name: Incitement and normalization
indicators.note: The DHS 'Worst of the Worst' campaign (see indicator 2) marks a concrete escalation from the more abstract framing concerns flagged in prior weeks: a senior administration official is now naming individual sitting judges by name, which multiple outlets and the judiciary itself describe as a materially different and more dangerous form of normalization given documented cases of judges being attacked over specific rulings.

indicators.name: Protest-related violence
indicators.note: No major new violent clash at ICE-related protests was confirmed within the window in vetted sourcing; ongoing 24/7 anti-ICE demonstrations in Portland and Los Angeles continued with routine arrests but no newly reported injuries or property destruction with injury risk this week. Carried at baseline.

indicators.note: DOJ obtained a 37-month federal sentence against Ismael Vega for a June 2025 attack on CHP officers during an anti-ICE protest (rock- and burning-debris-throwing from an overpass), and the Manhattan DA's office secured hate-crime charges and no-bail detention in the Upper West Side stabbing case; both show continued prosecutorial follow-through, though neither newly tests even-handed application across ideological targets this week.

indicators.note: No new survey data this week; carried forward at baseline. The DHS campaign naming judges by name is scored under indicators 2 (PVEI) and 4 (SCI) rather than here, to avoid double-counting the same fact pattern.

weeks.relationship_note: Violence-pressure indicators eased slightly on the absence of a new completed/attempted/foiled attack, but a senior federal official's decision to publicly name individual sitting judges — met with alarm from the judiciary itself but no clearly documented cross-aisle political condemnation — kept both the threats/incitement side of PVEI and the leadership-rhetoric side of SCI moving in an unfavorable direction, narrowing but not closing the gap.

event_log.target: U.S. District Judges Matthew Kennelly, Allison Burroughs, Paula Xinis, and Hernán Vera
event_log.action: Publicly named and criticized four sitting federal district judges by name in a social-media series titled 'Worst of the Worst, District Judge Edition,' accusing them of 'open defiance' of the Supreme Court and 'naked political activism' over rulings that blocked administration immigration policies. Judge Esther Salas — whose 20-year-old son was murdered in 2020 by a litigant angry over her rulings — publicly stated the campaign was 'so dangerous' and that she was 'more concerned right now than I was after my only child was murdered.'
event_log.notes: Scored under both the PVEI incitement/normalization indicator and the SCI leadership-rhetoric indicator because the same fact pattern speaks to both climate-normalization risk and the absence of cross-aisle condemnation; not double-counted within either index. Also logged, separately, under the PVEI threats-against-judges indicator in the indicator note rather than as a second event-log entry, since it is the same underlying episode. No corresponding statement of bipartisan congressional condemnation of the campaign was identified in available sourcing as of this report.

event_log.actor: U.S. District Court, Central District of California (Judge John F. Walter) / DOJ
event_log.target: Ismael Vega (defendant); underlying target of original 2025 offense was CHP officers
event_log.action: Sentenced Ismael Vega, 42, to 37 months in federal prison and $253,415 in restitution for throwing rocks and lit burning debris onto a CHP vehicle from a downtown Los Angeles freeway overpass during a June 8, 2025 anti-ICE protest, trapping officers below and creating a risk of death or serious injury; Vega pleaded guilty April 29 to obstructing law enforcement during civil disorder.
event_log.notes: The underlying violent act occurred in June 2025 and was not newly counted against this week's protest-related-violence score (pvei_effect: neutral); the sentencing itself is logged as a positive prosecutorial-follow-through signal for SCI.

event_log.actor: Raul Morales (defendant) / Manhattan District Attorney's Office
event_log.target: A 57-year-old Asian man and a 50-year-old Jewish man, stabbed in separate incidents blocks apart on Manhattan's Upper West Side
event_log.action: Morales was arraigned July 24 on hate-crime counts including attempted second-degree murder as a hate crime for both stabbings and held without bail; witnesses reported he yelled 'Allahu Akbar' and 'justice for Islam' during the attacks. Case remained in active prosecution through this reporting window.
event_log.notes: The stabbings themselves occurred July 23, just before this tracker's reporting window (and were not covered by a prior weekly report, since no report was produced for week 30/July 20-26). Included here because the case's hate-crime prosecution was actively developing through the current window and materially informs this week's hate-crimes indicator status; not scored as a new attack this week (pvei_effect: neutral) to avoid overstating a within-window escalation.

weeks.trajectory_note: Note on continuity: no weekly report was produced for week 30 (July 20-26, 2026), so this entry compares directly against week 29 (July 13-19) rather than an unbroken prior week; readers should treat the week-over-week point changes as spanning roughly two weeks of underlying developments rather than one. Over that span, the clearest through-line is a shift in the character of institutional pressure on the judiciary: last period's concern was broad framing documents (the Bondi memo, NSPM-7) and general warnings from justices about rising threat volume; this period saw a senior DHS official personally naming four sitting judges by name and accusing them of political activism, which the judiciary itself — including a judge who has lived through the worst-case outcome of that kind of personalized targeting — described as materially more dangerous than generic rhetoric. That is organized, institutional incitement risk, not lone-actor violence, and it was not met with identified cross-aisle political condemnation this week, even as it was met with real prosecutorial follow-through on unrelated protest-violence and hate-crime cases. Violence/threat activity this period is diffuse rather than concentrated: no single high-severity plot or attack anchors the week, unlike the prior period's foiled White House UFC plot, which is itself a modest positive data point. The gap narrowed slightly (from -8 to -5) primarily because PVEI eased on the absence of a new violent incident, not because social cohesion strengthened — cohesion in fact weakened slightly on the leadership-rhetoric indicator. Watch next: whether the DHS judge-naming campaign is followed by any bipartisan congressional response (its absence so far is itself informative), and whether it correlates with any new increase in threats reported by the Marshals Service in the next data cycle.

event_log.actor: Unidentified individuals conducting a sustained intimidation campaign; background context includes Rep. Greg Steube and Rep. Andrew Clyde (pending impeachment resolutions)
event_log.target: U.S. District Judge John J. McConnell Jr. (D.R.I.) and his family
event_log.action: Judge McConnell publicly detailed, in Washington Post and other reporting, at least six credible death threats and a 'pizza doxxing' incident (an unsolicited pizza ordered to his home in the name of Daniel Anderl, the murdered son of Judge Esther Salas) received since his 2025 ruling blocking the Trump administration's federal funding freeze; threats intensified after activist Laura Loomer and Elon Musk amplified posts naming him and his daughter.
event_log.notes: The underlying threat campaign began in 2025 and was reported in earlier pizza-doxxing coverage; what is new this week is McConnell's detailed public account. Two House Republicans have separately introduced impeachment resolutions against McConnell (H.Res.241; a second by Rep. Clyde) over his rulings, not over the threats themselves; no identified statement of bipartisan congressional condemnation of the threats was found in available sourcing.

event_log.notes: The underlying shooting occurred July 16, 2026, before this reporting window and before the prior week's report; not scored as a new incident this week (pvei_effect: neutral). Congressional accountability push this week came only from Democratic members; no bipartisan statement was identified.

event_log.notes: Victims sustained non-life-threatening injuries; same-night arrest logged as a positive prosecutorial-response signal alongside the negative PVEI hate-crime signal from the underlying assault.

event_log.target: Gerald Pitts (defendant); underlying 2023 victim Santos Tejas Gonzalez

weeks.trajectory_note: Violence/threat activity this week remained diffuse rather than concentrated: no single high-severity plot or attack anchored the period, continuing the pattern from week 31. The clearest through-line remains judiciary-focused: Judge McConnell's public account of sustained threats and 'pizza doxxing' corroborates rather than newly escalates the picture established last week by the DHS judge-naming campaign, while separate, ongoing House impeachment resolutions against him (introduced by individual Republican members over his rulings, not connected to the threats and not joined by a bipartisan rebuke of the threats themselves) illustrate that institutional and extralegal pressure on judges are running on parallel tracks. This is organized/systemic institutional pressure rather than lone-actor violence, and it continues to go unmet by any identified cross-aisle congressional condemnation of the threats specifically. Encouragingly, prosecutorial follow-through was unusually visible this week across three independent cases (Seattle, Los Angeles, and the ongoing Aurora prosecution), and a large civic-engagement event (National Night Out) provided a modest, if not decisive, positive counter-data point. Local journalism capacity continued to erode, a slow-moving negative trend for the information-ecosystem indicator rather than a new shock.\n\nNet effect: PVEI edges up modestly on the fresh Seattle hate-crime incident and the reinforced threats/incitement narrative around the judiciary; SCI edges up slightly more on strong prosecutorial signals and the National Night Out data point, partially offset by continued local-news contraction. The gap narrows marginally from -5 to -4 — still a manageable-strain reading rather than a dangerous imbalance. Watch next: whether the McConnell disclosures prompt any bipartisan congressional response, and whether U.S. Marshals Service FY2026 year-end figures confirm the trajectory toward exceeding FY2025's 564 judicial threats.
